items.title: Loren Schoenberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2019
items.q: I learned a lot from reading Albert Murray and then getting to know him

ctx.x: Because I mean, I’m a college dropout so let’s get that straight. So I don’t know a lot of terms to be conversant with necessarily, and I might be confusing some that someone with an academic background might hear me talking and right now they’re rolling their eyes. But what I mean is that — well you mentioned teaching jazz history. We don’t get to Jelly Roll Morton or Sidney Bechet for a couple of months. So you know it’s all about New Orleans and English and French mercantilism, and what it was like to be…

lot from reading Albert Murray and then getting to know him and Stanley Crouch and others, and just doing a lot of reading and talking to people, including musicians of the much older generations. I mean I got to know Zutty Singleton’s wife pretty well, which I’ll talk about when we talk about the New York Jazz Museum, and trying to put it all together in some way that makes sense. So I don’t know if that answered your question.
